name: Bhurja

name: Bijapura

name: Matsyakshi

name: Mayurashikha

name: Bhadra
description: In Ayurveda, Bhadra is traditionally used to balance Pitta and Kapha doshas. Classical texts describe it as possessing Tikta (bitter) and Kashaya (astringent) tastes with a Laghu (light) quality. It has a Sheeta (cooling) virya and Katu (pungent) vipaka, and may increase Vata dosha.

name: Bhumi Jambuka
description: In Ayurveda, Bhumi Jambuka is traditionally used to balance Vata and Kapha doshas. Classical texts describe it as possessing a bitter taste (Tikta Rasa), light quality (Laghu Guna), heating potency (Ushna Virya), and a pungent post-digestive effect (Katu Vipaka). Its roots and leaves are traditionally utilized to support joint comfort and ease internal Vata movement.

name: Bhutika
description: In Ayurveda, Bhutika, commonly known as Lemongrass, is traditionally used to support digestive warmth and clear excess Kapha. Classical texts describe its leaves and oil as possessing pungent and bitter tastes (Katu and Tikta Rasa), light and sharp qualities (Laghu and Tikshna Guna), and heating energy (Ushna Virya), which help calm internal Vata.

name: Chakragaja
description: In Ayurveda, Chakragaja is traditionally used to support urinary system balance and soothe excess heat. Classical texts describe its seeds and leaves as having a sweet taste (Madhura Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), and cooling potency (Sheeta Virya). These inherent properties serve to gently balance Pitta and Kapha doshas.

name: Chhatraka
description: In Ayurveda, Chhatraka is traditionally used as a deeply grounding, nourishing substance that supports physical strength. Classical texts describe the whole plant as having a sweet taste (Madhura Rasa), heavy and unctuous qualities (Guru and Snigdha Guna), and cooling energy (Sheeta Virya), which naturally pacify Vata dosha while potentially increasing Pitta and Kapha.

name: Dhamargava
description: In Ayurveda, Dhamargava is traditionally used to clear excess Kapha and Pitta from internal channels. Classical texts describe its fruits, seeds, and roots as possessing a bitter taste (Tikta Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), heating potency (Ushna Virya), and a pungent post-digestive effect (Katu Vipaka).

name: Gavedhuka
description: In Ayurveda, Gavedhuka is traditionally used to support tissue balance and clear accumulated fluid channels. Classical texts describe its seeds and roots as possessing sweet and astringent tastes (Madhura and Kashaya Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), heating potency (Ushna Virya), and a sweet post-digestive effect, aiding in balancing Pitta and Kapha.

name: Kshavaka
description: In Ayurveda, Kshavaka is traditionally used to clear upper respiratory channels and stimulate the sense organs. Classical texts describe the whole plant as having a pungent taste (Katu Rasa), sharp and light qualities (Tikshna and Laghu Guna), heating potency (Ushna Virya), and a pungent post-digestive nature, which actively pacify Vata and Kapha.

name: Kurabaka
description: In Ayurveda, Kurabaka is traditionally used to support tissue comfort and soothe localized swelling. Classical texts describe its whole plant and roots as possessing a bitter taste (Tikta Rasa), light quality (Laghu Guna), heating energy (Ushna Virya), and a pungent post-digestive effect (Katu Vipaka), making it ideal for balancing Vata and Kapha doshas.

name: Mamsarohini
description: In Ayurveda, Mamsarohini is traditionally used to support tissue cohesion, firm loose structures, and calm fluid discharge. Classical texts describe its bark as having an astringent taste (Kashaya Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), cooling potency (Sheeta Virya), and a pungent post-digestive effect (Katu Vipaka), which effectively pacify Pitta and Kapha.

name: Medasaka
description: In Ayurveda, Medasaka is traditionally used to support tissue soothing and comfort structural regions. Classical texts describe its bark and leaves as having sweet and astringent tastes (Madhura and Kashaya Rasa), heavy and unctuous qualities (Guru and Snigdha Guna), and heating potency (Ushna Virya). These properties serve to deeply balance Vata and Pitta doshas.

name: Aivana
description: In Ayurveda, Aivana is traditionally used to soothe hyperactive Vata and quiet internal tension. Classical texts describe its seeds as possessing bitter and pungent tastes (Tikta and Katu Rasa), heavy and dry qualities (Guru and Ruksha Guna), heating energy (Ushna Virya), and a pungent post-digestive nature, contributing to the pacification of Vata and Kapha.

name: Asphota
description: In Ayurveda, Asphota is traditionally used to support mental clarity, calm the mind, and balance neurological pathways. Classical texts describe its roots, seeds, and leaves as having bitter and astringent tastes (Tikta and Kashaya Rasa), a light quality (Laghu Guna), and cooling energy (Sheeta Virya), which harmoniously balance Vata and Pitta.

name: Abhishuka
description: In Ayurveda, Abhishuka is traditionally used to support physical stamina, nourish vital tissues, and calm dry Vata. Classical texts describe its seeds as having sweet and astringent tastes (Madhura and Kashaya Rasa), heavy and unctuous qualities (Guru and Snigdha Guna), heating energy (Ushna Virya), and a sweet post-digestive effect (Madhura Vipaka).

name: Muranji
description: In Ayurveda, Muranji is traditionally used to support deep channel clearing and melt dense internal accumulations. Classical texts describe its bark, roots, and seeds as having pungent and bitter tastes (Katu and Tikta Rasa), light, dry, and sharp qualities (Laghu, Ruksha, and Tikshna Guna), and heating energy (Ushna Virya), effectively pacifying Vata and Kapha.

name: Mayaphala
description: In Ayurveda, Mayaphala is traditionally used to support firm tissue tone, maintain fluid balance, and soothe mucous membranes. Classical texts describe the fruit gall as possessing a dominant astringent taste (Kashaya Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), and cooling potency (Sheeta Virya), which strongly balance Pitta and Kapha doshas.

name: Kankra
description: In Ayurveda, Kankra is traditionally used to support mucosal integrity and bind excessive fluids within internal pathways. Classical texts describe its bark as having astringent and bitter tastes (Kashaya and Tikta Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), and cooling energy (Sheeta Virya), serving to effectively pacify Pitta and Kapha.

name: Sadapushpi
description: In Ayurveda, Sadapushpi is traditionally used to balance internal metabolic heat and clear excess channel fluid. Classical texts describe its leaves and roots as possessing a bitter taste (Tikta Rasa), light and dry qualities (Laghu and Ruksha Guna), cooling potency (Sheeta Virya), and a pungent post-digestive effect (Katu Vipaka), which balance Pitta and Kapha.

name: Sahachara
description: In Ayurveda, Sahachara is traditionally used to support lower body movement, joint flexibility, and neurological strength. Classical texts describe the whole plant and root as having bitter and sweet tastes (Tikta and Madhura Rasa), light and smooth qualities (Laghu and Snigdha Guna), and heating potency (Ushna Virya), making it ideal for balancing Vata and Kapha.
